fullPassage: To the ancients, looking out at the night sky, the Universe seemed eternal and unchanging. Right up until the 1920s, what we now know to be the Milky Way galaxy, an island of a few hundred billion stars, was thought to be the entire Universe, in which individual stars might be born, live and die but the overall appearance always remained the same, like a forest in which individual trees live and die without changing the overall appearance. The idea of an unchanging Universe was so deeply rooted that even Albert Einstein, usually willing to entertain new ideas, accepted it without question. When he applied the equations of his general theory of relativity to describe the behaviour of the entire Universe (all of space and time), he found that the mathematics said that the Universe could not be static, but must be either expanding or contracting. This seemed so improbable to him that he added an extra factor to the equations, called the cosmological constant, to hold everything still.

When he applied the equations of his general theory of relativity to describe the behaviour of the entire Universe (all of space and time), he found that the mathematics said that the Universe could not be (B)[active / static], but must be either expanding or contracting. This seemed so (C)[improbable / reasonable] to him that he added an extra factor to the equations, called the cosmological constant, to hold everything still.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우주는 영원하고(eternal) 변하지 않는 것처럼 보였고, 수학은 우주가 정적일(static) 수 없다고 했으며, 우주가 팽창·수축한다는 결과는 아인슈타인에게 있을 법하지 않게(improbable) 여겨졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① eternal — static — improbable — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② temporary — static — improbable (A 반대: 영원한→일시적인)
❌ ③ eternal — active — improbable (B 반대: 정적인→활발한)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"remaining in one place or state without moving, changing, or developing"

det.korean: 움직이거나 변하거나 발전하지 않고 한 상태에 머무르는 → static(정적인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① dynamic — 역동적인 (정의와 반대)
❌ ② distant — 멀리 있는 (정의와 무관)
❌ ③ crowded — 붐비는 (정의와 무관)
✅ ④ static — 정적인, 움직이지 않는 ←정답
det.tip: static = 움직임·변화가 없는 (dynamic의 반대)

questions.passage: To the ancients, __________ (look) out at the night sky, the Universe seemed eternal and unchanging. The idea of an unchanging Universe was so deeply rooted that even Albert Einstein, usually willing to entertain new ideas, accepted it without question.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: 주절의 주어(the ancients)가 '밤하늘을 바라보는' 동작을 동시에 하는 상황이므로, 분사구문을 만드는 현재분사 looking으로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: To the ancients, __________ (look) out at the night sky, ... → 문장 앞에서 '~하면서'로 이어지는 분사구문 자리 → look을 현재분사 looking으로
det.tip: 분사구문: Looking out ... = 밤하늘을 바라보면서

questions.passage: To the ancients, looking out at the night sky, the Universe seemed eternal and unchanging. Right up until the 1920s, the Milky Way galaxy was thought to be the entire Universe, in which individual stars might be __________ (bear), live and die but the overall appearance always remained the same.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: 별이 '태어나는' 대상이므로 「might be + 과거분사」 수동태가 되어야 한다. 동사 bear의 과거분사는 불규칙형 born이다.
det.analysis: individual stars might be __________ (bear) → 「조동사 might + be + 과거분사」 수동태 = 태어나게 되다 → bear의 과거분사 born
det.tip: bear(낳다) → 과거분사 born (불규칙)

questions.passage: To the ancients, looking out at the night sky, the Universe seemed eternal and unchanging. Right up until the 1920s, what we now know to be the Milky Way galaxy, an island of a few hundred billion stars, was thought to be the entire Universe, in which individual stars might be born, live and die but the overall appearance always remained the same, like a forest in which individual trees live and die without changing the overall appearance. The idea of an unchanging Universe was so deeply rooted that even Albert Einstein, usually willing to entertain new ideas, accepted it without question. When he applied the equations of his general theory of relativity to describe the behaviour of the entire Universe (all of space and time), he found that the mathematics said that the Universe could not be static, but must be either __________. This seemed so improbable to him that he added an extra factor to the equations, called the cosmological constant, to hold everything still.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수학은 우주가 정적일(static) 수 없다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 정적 상태와 반대되는 '팽창하거나 수축하는(expanding or contracting)' 상태가 들어가야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① expanding or contracting — 팽창하거나 수축하는, static의 반대 ←정답
❌ ② bright or dark — 밝거나 어두운 (움직임·크기와 무관)
❌ ③ old or new — 오래되거나 새로운 (문맥 무관)
❌ ④ near or far — 가깝거나 먼 (문맥 무관)
det.tip: could not be static, but must be either ______ = 정적일 수 없고 팽창·수축해야 한다

questions.passage: To the ancients, looking out at the night sky, the Universe seemed eternal and unchanging. Right up until the 1920s, what we now know to be the Milky Way galaxy, an island of a few hundred billion stars, was thought to be the entire Universe, in which individual stars might be born, live and die but the overall appearance always remained the same, like a forest in which individual trees live and die without changing the overall appearance. The idea of an unchanging Universe was so deeply rooted that even Albert Einstein, usually willing to entertain new ideas, accepted it without question. When he applied the equations of his general theory of relativity to describe the behaviour of the entire Universe (all of space and time), he found that the mathematics said that the Universe could not be static, but must be either expanding or contracting. This seemed so improbable to him that he added an extra factor to the equations, called the cosmological constant, to __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 아인슈타인은 변하지 않는 우주를 믿었으므로, 우주 상수를 더한 목적은 '모든 것을 정지 상태로 유지하는(hold everything still)' 것이었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① speed up its expansion — 팽창을 가속하다 (정적 우주를 원한 의도와 반대)
✅ ② hold everything still — 모든 것을 정지 상태로 유지하다 ←정답
❌ ③ create new galaxies — 새 은하를 만들다 (본문에 없음)
❌ ④ measure the starlight — 별빛을 측정하다 (본문에 없음)
det.tip: cosmological constant, to hold everything still = 모든 것을 정지시키기 위한 우주 상수
